entities.summary: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano is a Mexican politician and civil engineer. A prominent social-democrat and the son of 51st president of Mexico Lázaro Cárdenas, he is a former Head of Government of Mexico City and a founder of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD). He ran for the presidency of Mexico three times, and his loss in the 1988 Mexican general election to Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) candidate Carlos Salinas de Gortari had long been considered the result of electoral fraud perpetrated by the ruling PRI, later acknowledged by Miguel de la Madrid, the incumbent president at the time of the election.

entities.summary:
Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano, born May 1, 1934, in Mexico City, stands as a seminal figure in Mexico's late 20th-century democratic transition. A distinguished civil engineer and politician, he is the revered son of Lázaro Cárdenas del Río, Mexico's 51st president, and became a central architect of multi-party democracy, directly challenging the entrenched, decades-long hegemony of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI). His political career, marked by a commitment to social justice and electoral transparency, fundamentally reshaped the landscape of Mexican politics and governance.

Initially a member of the PRI, Cárdenas Solórzano broke away in the mid-1980s to form the Democratic Current, advocating for internal party reform and greater democratic openness. This dissent culminated in his presidential candidacy in the 1988 Mexican general election, a contest widely considered fraudulent due to a notorious 'system crash' on election night that halted vote counting, ultimately declaring Carlos Salinas de Gortari of the PRI the victor amidst national and international outcry. Following this contentious election, Cárdenas Solórzano co-founded the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) in 1989, consolidating a powerful left-wing opposition. He subsequently ran for president in 1994 and 2000, and served as the first democratically elected Head of Government of Mexico City from 1997 to 1999, implementing significant social and infrastructure programs.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano's leadership fundamentally challenged Mexico's one-party system, leading to the establishment of the PRD and catalyzing electoral reforms that paved the way for pluralistic democracy. His actions directly contributed to the end of the PRI's 71-year presidential rule in 2000.
